tags.name: TV
tags.description: Retro "virtual TV": lineups (ordered program sources), channels that play a lineup on a deterministic schedule (optionally shuffled), now-playing and the program guide.

tags.name: TV Feeds
tags.description: Integrations for external players and media servers: M3U playlist, XMLTV guide, MPEG-TS live streams and HDHomeRun tuner emulation (Plex, Jellyfin, VLC, Kodi).

A lineup is an ordered list of program sources (files, shows, seasons, folders, library queries). Channels play lineups.

409 `conflict` (with `details.channels`: the channel ids) while channels use the lineup, unless `force=1`, which deletes those channels too.

put.description:
Replaces the ordered item list (at most 5000). Items that echo an existing `id` keep it. Only the owner may change a lineup (403 for a shared one).

**Scope:** `tv:write`

post.description:
Inserts items at `position` (default: append). A lineup holds at most 5000 items. Only the owner may change a lineup (403 for a shared one).

**Scope:** `tv:write`

get.description:
Expansion of API.md §7.1 step 1 with the lineup owner's permissions. Skipped files are reported with a reason. Cached in memory; invalidated on lineup changes, file events and after 2 minutes.

**Scope:** `tv:read`

The caller's channels plus shared channels, sorted by number.

post.description:
`lineup_id` must be one of the caller's own lineups (404 otherwise). The number is auto-assigned (highest + 1) when omitted; 409 when taken. `shuffle_seed` is generated server-side and never exposed.

**Scope:** `tv:write`

patch.description:
Owner only (403 for someone else's shared channel). 409 when the new number is taken; 422 when `lineup_id` is not one of the caller's lineups.

**Scope:** `tv:write`

put.description:
Raw JPEG, PNG or GIF body (≤ 20 MiB, ≤ 50 megapixels; format detected from the content, not the Content-Type). The image is decoded and re-encoded server-side as a JPEG of at most 512 px; anything else (WebP, SVG, …) is 415.

**Scope:** `tv:write`

Picks a new random shuffle seed so the channel feels fresh. Viewers jump to whatever the new order puts on air now.

**Scope:** `tv:write`

get.description:
Live channels: the deterministic broadcast position (same for every viewer). On-demand channels: the caller's saved position (`PUT …/position`); it does not advance while nobody watches.

**Scope:** `tv:read`

Range-capable byte stream of a program (`Program.stream_url` always uses this form). Authorised by the **channel** (the caller owns it or it is `shared`) and by the file being part of the channel's expanded lineup — viewers of a shared channel need no read access to the owner's files. Any other file ID answers 404. The narrower scope `tv:feed` (feed tokens) is accepted too.

**Scope:** `tv:read` · also accepts `?access_token=`

parameters.name: file_id
parameters.description: File ID of a program in the channel's expanded lineup.

206.description: Partial content for a satisfiable `Range` request.

get.description:
ffmpeg H.264/AAC fragmented-MP4 variant of the program stream (`Program.transcode_url`); not seekable — request again with a new `start`. 501 `ffmpeg_unavailable` without ffmpeg. Shares the media transcode limits, charged to the **caller** (not the channel owner): two transcodes server-wide and one per user, waiting up to 5 s for a slot before 429; a client that stops reading for 60 s is dropped. Authorised by the **channel** (the caller owns it or it is `shared`) and by the file being part of the channel's expanded lineup — viewers of a shared channel need no read access to the owner's files. Any other file ID answers 404.

**Scope:** `tv:read` · also accepts `?access_token=`

parameters.name: file_id
parameters.description: File ID of a program in the channel's expanded lineup.

get.description:
Poster (custom, else the generated thumbnail) of a program of the channel, served with the channel owner's permissions. `size` other than sm/md/lg is 422.

**Scope:** `tv:read` · also accepts `?access_token=`

parameters.name: file_id
parameters.description: File ID of a program in the channel's expanded lineup.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Size class (`sm` 160 px, `md` 320 px, `lg` 640 px longest edge).

Authorised by the **channel** (the caller owns it or it is `shared`) and by the file being part of the channel's expanded lineup — viewers of a shared channel need no read access to the owner's files. Any other file ID answers 404.

**Scope:** `tv:read` · also accepts `?access_token=`

parameters.name: file_id

put.description:
Only for `playback_mode: on_demand` channels: stores where the caller is (program index in the cycle and offset). Per-user state, so read scope suffices.

**Scope:** `tv:read`

get.description:
Programs overlapping the window per channel (the first may have started before `start`). On-demand channels show the caller's own continuation from their saved position (programs back to back from now on). At most 20 000 programs per response.

**Scope:** `tv:read`

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Guide start (RFC 3339, within a year of now; default: now rounded down to 30 minutes).

parameters.name: hours
parameters.description: Window length in hours (1–72, fractions allowed).

parameters.name: channel_ids
parameters.description: Comma-separated channel IDs (default: all visible channels; at most 200 channels per response).

post.description:
Builds lineups and channels from the library in one go (one channel per show, per genre, all movies, or all TV). Numbers are auto-assigned.

**Scope:** `tv:write`

get.description:
Creates the feed token on first call: a personal access token with only the scope `tv:feed`, which reaches the M3U and XMLTV feeds, channel logos, `live.ts`, `play`, program streams and the HDHomeRun emulation, and nothing else (no lineups, channels, guide, positions, posters, subtitles or transcodes, no media library). The caller's credential must hold `tv:read` (403 otherwise), so a narrower token cannot reveal a broader one. Feed tokens minted earlier carried `media:read` and later `tv:read`; they are narrowed to `tv:feed` in place on upgrade (URLs keep working), a `tv:read`-only one is still accepted until the URLs are rotated, and one found with any other scopes is replaced.

**Scope:** `tv:read`

post.description:
Revokes the current feed token and mints a new one (every old feed URL stops working). The caller's credential must also hold `tv:read`.

**Scope:** `tv:write`

get.description:
M3U playlist of the caller's visible channels with `tvg-id` (channel id), `tvg-chno`, `tvg-name`, `tvg-logo` and `group-title`. Stream URLs point to `live.ts` when ffmpeg is available, else to `/play`. URLs embed the request's own `access_token` (or, for cookie/bearer requests, the user's feed token). The narrower scope `tv:feed` (feed tokens) is accepted too.

**Scope:** `tv:read` · also accepts `?access_token=`

XMLTV guide for `tv.guide_days` days from the current hour (live schedules; at most 10 000 programmes per channel). Channel ids match the M3U `tvg-id`. The narrower scope `tv:feed` (feed tokens) is accepted too.

**Scope:** `tv:read` · also accepts `?access_token=`

Plays the channel like a broadcast: the current program from the live offset, then the following ones, each transcoded by ffmpeg (720p H.264/AAC) into one continuous MPEG-TS stream with increasing timestamps. On-demand channels use their live schedule here. `501 ffmpeg_unavailable` without ffmpeg; 429 when all tuners are busy (per user: `tv.hdhr_tuner_count`; 16 server-wide). Stops when the client disconnects or stops reading for 30 s. The narrower scope `tv:feed` (feed tokens) is accepted too.

**Scope:** `tv:read` · also accepts `?access_token=`

302 to the current program's channel-scoped stream URL with `#t=<offset>` (on-demand channels: the caller's position). When the request used `?access_token=`, the redirect carries it. 404 when nothing is on air. The narrower scope `tv:feed` (feed tokens) is accepted too.

**Scope:** `tv:read` · also accepts `?access_token=`

Location.description: Stream URL of the current program, e.g. `/api/v1/tv/channels/<id>/programs/<file_id>/stream?access_token=…#t=312.4`.

Plex and Jellyfin POST `lineup.post?scan=start` while adding the tuner. The lineup is always current, so this only acknowledges the request with an empty 200. Same 404 rules as the other HDHomeRun endpoints.

**Scope:** `public`

TvLineupQuery.description: `kind=query`: library filter (same semantics as `GET /api/v1/media`). Empty strings are ignored.

TvLineupItem.description: One program source of a lineup. Which fields apply depends on `kind`.

kind.description: Source type: `file` (one file), `show` (all episodes of a show), `season` (one season of a show), `folder` (media files under a folder), `query` (library query).

path.description: `kind=folder`: folder path in the space (`""` = the space root; no `.`/`..` segments).

order.description: `default` keeps the natural order (episodes by season/episode/title, folders by natural path order, queries by show/sort title then season/episode); `random` shuffles within this item every cycle (deterministically, from the channel seed).

limit.description: Use at most this many playable files from the item (with `random`, a fixed pseudo-random subset).

label.description: Optional label shown in the editor.

TvLineupItemInput.description: A lineup item to create. Fields that do not apply to `kind` are ignored.

id.description: `PUT …/items` only: id of an existing item of this lineup to keep (ignored elsewhere).

kind.description: Source type: `file` (one file), `show` (all episodes of a show), `season` (one season of a show), `folder` (media files under a folder), `query` (library query).

path.description: `kind=folder`: folder path in the space (`""` = the space root; no `.`/`..` segments).

order.description: `default` keeps the natural order (episodes by season/episode/title, folders by natural path order, queries by show/sort title then season/episode); `random` shuffles within this item every cycle (deterministically, from the channel seed).

limit.description: Use at most this many playable files from the item (with `random`, a fixed pseudo-random subset).

label.description: Optional label shown in the editor.

item_count.description: Number of playable files after expansion.

items.description: Full ordered replacement (at most 5000 items per lineup). Echo an existing item's `id` to keep its identity (and the seed of its `random` order); other items get new ids.

position.description: 0-based insert position; omit (or pass a value past the end) to append.

title.description: Display title (`Show · S1E2 · Episode` for episodes).

file_id.description: The skipped file (for `not_found`: the lineup item id).

reason.description: `unreadable`: missing, trashed or not readable by the lineup owner; `unknown_duration`: no (or a zero) duration yet; `not_found`: a folder item whose folder does not exist or is not readable.

source_item_id.description: Lineup item the file came from.

TvLineupExpanded.description: The lineup expanded to playable files in default order (items with `order: random` appear in natural order here; channels shuffle them per cycle). Expansion uses the lineup owner's read permissions. A source referenced by several items (same file, show, season, folder or query) is looked up once.

skipped.description: Skipped files, at most the first 1 000 (`skipped_count` has the total).

skipped_count.description: Number of skipped files (may exceed the length of `skipped`).

truncated.description: True when a resource limit stopped the expansion before the end of the lineup: 50 000 playable files, or 100 000 files examined in all (every item and each file it yields counts, playable or not, repeated sources included). Later items contribute nothing.

shuffle_mode.description: `per_cycle`: a new (deterministic) order every time the lineup loops; `fixed`: one shuffled order until reshuffled.

playback_mode.description: `live`: everyone sees the same thing at the same time (like broadcast TV); `on_demand`: each user resumes where they left off.

visibility.description: `private`: only the owner; `shared`: listed for and playable by every user of this server (through channel-scoped program URLs, without access to the owner's files).

number.description: Omit to auto-assign the next free number.

visibility.description: `private`: only the owner; `shared`: listed for and playable by every user of this server (through channel-scoped program URLs, without access to the owner's files).

poster_url.description: Relative channel-scoped poster URL (`/api/v1/tv/channels/{id}/programs/{file_id}/poster?size=md`); `null` when no poster or thumbnail is available.

stream_url.description: Relative channel-scoped direct stream URL (`/api/v1/tv/channels/{id}/programs/{file_id}/stream`). Viewers of shared channels need no read access to the owner's files.

transcode_url.description: Relative channel-scoped transcode URL (`…/programs/{file_id}/transcode`); `null` without ffmpeg.

subtitles.description: Subtitle tracks (sidecar files and embedded text tracks; embedded ones only when ffmpeg is available). At most 32 per program; empty when there are none.

program.description: `null` when nothing is on air (empty lineup).

offset_seconds.description: Seconds into `program` — seek the player here (live: the broadcast position; on_demand: the caller's saved position).

index.description: Absolute program counter of `program` (`cycle × n + position in the cycle`); `null` when nothing is on air. On `on_demand` channels send it back with `PUT …/position`.

offset_seconds.description: Seconds into that program; at or past its end the next program starts.

strategy.description: `per_show`: one channel per show; `per_genre`: one per movie genre; `movies`: one all-movies channel; `all_tv`: one channel with every episode. Shows/genres whose name matches an existing channel of the caller are skipped, so repeating a call only adds new ones.

min_items.description: Skip shows/genres with fewer playable files.

TvFeeds.description: Feed URLs for external players. They embed a dedicated `lwp_` token with only `tv:read` (no `media:read`: a leaked feed URL can watch your channels and read their guide, but cannot list or stream the rest of your library) (listed among the account's tokens; revoking it there or rotating it here invalidates every URL) — treat them like passwords. Origin: `general.public_url` when set, else the request origin.

m3u_url.description: Absolute M3U playlist URL including the feed token.

xmltv_url.description: Absolute XMLTV guide URL including the feed token.

hdhr_url.description: HDHomeRun base URL (`…/api/v1/hdhr/<feed_token>`) when `tv.hdhr_enabled`, else `null`. Add it to Plex/Jellyfin as the tuner address.

TvHdhrDiscover.description: HDHomeRun `discover.json` (field names as expected by Plex/Jellyfin).

URL.description: Stream URL (`live.ts` with the feed token).

TvProgramSubtitle.description: A subtitle track of a program.

index.description: The media item's subtitle index (as in `media.subtitles`).

language.description: ISO 639-1 code (`en`, `pt-BR`) when known, else the tag as found; `""` when unknown.

label.description: Human-readable name (track title, or language plus flags).

url.description: Relative channel-scoped WebVTT URL (`/api/v1/tv/channels/{id}/programs/{file_id}/subtitles/{index}.vtt`). Viewers of shared channels need no read access to the owner's files.
